newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay says may resume some A330 services Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Cathay says may resume some A330 services Tuesday.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said some operation of its Airbus A330-300 aircraft could resume by Tuesday after a 10-day suspension, with the arrival of replacement parts on Monday.
"It is feasible that operations could commence tomorrow -- we're not definitive on that yet -- but certainly soon thereafter," Cathay spokesman Charlie Stewart-Cox told Reuters.

Cathay and its 25.5 percent-owned Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd (Dragonair) grounded their fleet of twin-engined A330-300 aircraft on May 24 after problems with Rolls-Royce Plc Trent 700 engines prompted a series of single-engine landings.
Cathay has 11 of the aircraft and Dragonair has four.
The problem stems from the lubrication system used in the Trent 700 gearbox, and Stewart-Cox said replacement modified parts had been approved by authorities in Britain and France.

Stewart-Cox said the replacement parts were arriving on Monday. Installation and testing would take place in Hong Kong and the airlines would be working with the territory's Civil Aviation Department, he said.
"We would hope that all aircraft would be able to re-enter services during the week of (beginning) June 9," he said.
Cathay chairman Peter Sutch said on Saturday that the grounding of its A330-300 fleet would slice between HK$120 million and HK$150 million from its bottom line this year.
The company earlier on Monday said it would be operating 89 percent of its flights for the day, after 11 flights were cancelled or combined with other flights.
"Despite the temporary suspension of our A330-300 services, Cathay Pacific will be operating 89 percent of its flights today," it said in a statement.
Cathay said charters had been arranged with Air Canada , Singapore Airlines and Air Mauritius .
